hidden_target.material_initial_state: An as-cast, nominally equiatomic WTaVTi refractory high-entropy alloy with a single-BCC, directionally solidified dendrite–interdendrite structure: W/Ta-rich dendrites (W37.5Ta28.9V17.8Ti15.8, ≈71 vol.%) and connected Ti/V-rich interdendritic channels (W9.9Ta17.7V35.8Ti36.6, ≈29 vol.%).
hidden_target.intervention: The WTaVTi precursor was subjected to liquid-metal dealloying by immersion in molten Cu at 1200 °C for 96 h. Ti-rich interdendritic regions were used as preferential sacrificial regions to create a directionally aligned RHEA–Cu composite. The precursor/RHEA dendrites were also screened by 25 keV He+ irradiation, and the composite's temperature-dependent thermal conductivity was measured.
hidden_target.conditions: The precursor and Cu were vacuum-sealed in silica and reacted at 1200 °C for 96 h; thermal conductivity was evaluated from room temperature to approximately 800 °C, with extrapolation above 1000 °C. Irradiation screening used 25 keV He+ implantation up to blistering fluences near 8–8.5 × 10^17 atoms cm−2, with swelling measured by AFM; irradiation behavior was measured on precursor dendrites as a proxy for the eventual RHEA ligaments, not directly on the full composite.
hidden_target.structural_mediator: A bicontinuous, directionally aligned structure containing ≈63.6 vol.% BCC RHEA ligaments (W31.5Ta30.9V21.4Ti14.3) and ≈36.4 vol.% nearly pure FCC Cu channels, with an approximately 300 nm spontaneously formed W-rich interlayer at every RHEA/Cu interface and minor HCP Ti-rich precipitates behind it.
hidden_target.mechanism: During liquid-metal dealloying, Ti has a negative heat of mixing with Cu and preferentially exchanges with Cu and dissolves from the Ti-rich interdendritic channels, whereas W, Ta, and V are comparatively immiscible with Cu and remain as RHEA ligaments. Continued interfacial Ti extraction leaves W, which has the strongest positive heat of mixing with Cu, trapped as a W-rich passivating interlayer that arrests further exchange and supports stable bonding. Aligned Cu channels provide conductive pathways; the increase in thermal conductivity with temperature is attributed to reduced diffuse interfacial mismatch and increasing lattice-mediated transport overcoming declining electronic transport. Reduced He-induced swelling is associated with the compositionally complex/distorted RHEA lattice and its high strength, which affect defect migration/recombination and improve resistance to blister cracking.
hidden_target.predicted_outcome: Relative to the low-conductivity WTaVTi precursor, Cu-channel formation was expected to raise thermal conductivity substantially, particularly at high temperature, ultimately allowing the composite to surpass pure W; relative to pure W, the WTaVTi RHEA ligaments were expected to show lower He-induced swelling and delayed blistering. High composite strength was anticipated from the continuous ≈64 vol.% RHEA network, but composite mechanical strength was not directly established in this study.
hidden_target.baseline: Thermal baselines were the unprocessed WTaVTi alloy, pure W, pure Cu, and reported conventional W–Cu composites. The primary irradiation baseline was pure W, with WTa and WTaV also tested for compositional comparison.
hidden_target.boundary: The selective replacement and aligned architecture hold for the directionally segregated WTaVTi precursor reacted under the reported 1200 °C/96 h LMD condition. The thermal advantage over pure W appears above approximately 650 °C; superiority over conventional W–Cu above 1000 °C is an extrapolated expectation. The irradiation conclusion is limited to low-energy, high-dose He+ screening of precursor dendrites and helium-induced swelling/blistering, not neutron irradiation, vacancy-driven void swelling, or direct testing of the finished composite.
hidden_target.discriminating_measurement: SEM/TEM-EDS and XRD were used to verify selective replacement, phase constitution, and the W-rich interface; laser-flash thermal analysis measured temperature-dependent thermal conductivity; 25 keV He+ implantation followed by AFM quantified swelling height and blister/crack onset versus fluence. Nanoindentation confirmed that the Cu-channel hardness was close to that of pure Cu.
hidden_target.actual_result: LMD replaced the interdendritic regions with >99 at.% Cu while retaining continuous RHEA ligaments, producing ≈63.6 vol.% RHEA and ≈36.4 vol.% Cu with millimeter-scale penetration, directional coherence of 0.274 versus 0.054 for a random composite, and an ≈300 nm W-rich interlayer. Composite thermal conductivity rose from ≈75 W m−1 K−1 at room temperature (4.4× the ≈17 W m−1 K−1 precursor value) with a +0.075 W m−1 K−2 slope to ≈120 W m−1 K−1 near 650 °C, where it surpassed pure W, and ≈140 W m−1 K−1 at 800 °C (over 85% of the rule-of-mixtures value). Under He+ irradiation, the WTaVTi precursor exhibited ≈108% swelling at blistering versus ≈137% for W—about 30% lower—and blistering/cracking was delayed from ≈8 × 10^17 atoms cm−2 for W to ≈8.5 × 10^17 atoms cm−2 for WTaVTi; at ≈4 × 10^17 atoms cm−2, swelling was ≈29.5% versus ≈32% for W, a difference the authors note may be insignificant.
